docs.title: Terminology Glossary
docs.text:
This glossary defines common terms used in software documentation and technical writing for DocEngine.

Term Definition Example Related Terms API A set of protocols and tools for building and interacting with software services. "Use the API to retrieve account data." Endpoint, Request, Response Authentication The process of verifying a user's identity before granting access. "Authenticate with an API key." Authorization, Login Authorization The process of granting access to specific resources or actions. "The token authorizes read-only access." Authentication, Permissions Backend The server-side logic and infrastructure that powers an application. "The backend processes incoming requests." Frontend, Server CLI A command-line interface used to run commands and scripts. "Run the CLI command to deploy the app." Terminal, Shell Code Block A section of text formatted to display source code clearly. "Use a fenced code block for shell commands." Syntax Highlighting, Markdown Configuration Settings that define how an application or service behaves. "Update the configuration file to change the port." Environment, Settings Dependency A package or module required by software to function correctly. "The project has a dependency on Flask." Package, Library Deployment The process of making an application available to users. "Deployment to production occurred at midnight." Release, Production Documentation Written information that explains how something works or how to use it. "The documentation includes setup steps." Guide, Reference Endpoint A specific URL or route exposed by an API. "The endpoint returns user profile data." API, Route Environment A runtime context such as development, staging, or production. "Use the staging environment for testing." Configuration, Deployment Error Message A notification that explains a problem or failure. "The error message says the token is expired." Exception, Warning Example A sample showing how something should be done or appear. "The example illustrates a successful request." Tutorial, Snippet Feature A distinct capability or function provided by software. "The feature allows exporting reports." Capability, Functionality Frontend The user-facing part of an application. "The frontend displays the dashboard." Backend, UI Git A version control system used to track changes in source code. "Commit the change with Git." Repository, Branch Guide A document that helps the reader perform a task. "Follow the guide to install the tool." Tutorial, Documentation Header Metadata or additional information placed at the top of a document or request. "The header contains the authorization token." Metadata, Request Input Data provided to a system or function. "The input field accepts an email address." Output, Parameter Installation The process of setting up software on a machine or environment. "Installation completed successfully." Setup, Configuration Integration The process of connecting systems or services so they work together. "The integration syncs the CRM with the app." Connector, API Issue A problem, bug, or task that needs attention. "The issue was reported by a customer." Bug, Ticket Library A reusable collection of code or functionality. "The library provides charting tools." Package, Dependency Markdown A lightweight markup language used to format text. "Write the page in Markdown." Formatting, Plain Text Metadata Descriptive information about a file, page, or record. "The metadata includes the author name." Header, Tag Navigation The structure that helps users move through content. "Navigation links lead to the setup page." Menu, Sidebar Parameter A named input used by a function, command, or API call. "The parameter sets the page size." Argument, Input Permissions The rights granted to users or services for specific actions. "Permissions control who can edit content." Authorization, Role Pipeline A sequence of automated steps used to build, test, or deploy software. "The pipeline runs tests after each commit." CI/CD, Workflow Preview A temporary view of content before publication. "Preview the page before publishing it." Draft, Local Server Release A version of software made available to users. "The release includes bug fixes and improvements." Deployment, Version Repository A storage location for code or documentation files. "The repository contains the project source." Git, Branch Request A message sent to a service or API to perform an action. "The request returned a 200 status code." Response, Endpoint Response The data or status returned after processing a request. "The response contains the created resource." Request, Payload Route A defined path that maps a URL to application logic. "The route handles user profile requests." Endpoint, Path Screenshot An image capture of a screen or interface. "The screenshot shows the dashboard view." Image, UI Search Index A structured collection of content used to make search fast and accurate. "The search index updates when content changes." Search, Indexing Server A system that hosts applications or services. "The server responds to client requests." Backend, Host Session A temporary interaction period between a user and an application. "The session expires after inactivity." Token, Login Snippet A small reusable example or fragment of code or text. "Use the snippet in the example section." Example, Template Syntax Highlighting Formatting that visually distinguishes code elements. "Syntax highlighting improves readability." Code Block, Markdown Template A reusable structure for creating consistent content. "The template defines the page layout." Snippet, Framework Terminal A text-based interface for running commands. "Open the terminal and run the command." CLI, Shell Token A credential or identifier used to authenticate access. "The token is passed in the authorization header." Authentication, Session UI The visual interface through which users interact with software. "The UI includes a sidebar and a toolbar." Frontend, UX UX The overall experience a user has while interacting with a product. "The UX is designed to minimize friction." UI, Usability Version A specific release or iteration of software. "Version 2.0 introduces a new dashboard." Release, Update Workflow A sequence of steps used to complete a task or process. "The workflow includes review and approval." Process, Pipeline

docs.title: Technical Documentation Style Guide
docs.text: This guide defines the voice, structure, and formatting standards for DocEngine documentation. Consistent writing helps readers scan content quickly, trust the information, and complete tasks with confidence.

docs.title: Voice and Tone
docs.text:
Write in a clear, direct, and professional tone.

  • Use plain language whenever possible.
  • Be concise and useful.
  • Address the reader as "you" when giving instructions.
  • Favor active voice over passive voice.
  • Keep the tone helpful, calm, and confident.

Example:

  • Prefer: "Create a new project by running the command below."
  • Avoid: "A new project can be created by running the command below."

docs.title: Grammar Rules
docs.text:
Follow these grammar standards:

  • Use standard American English.
  • Use present tense for procedures and descriptions.
  • Use second person for instructions: "Click", "Open", "Enter".
  • Use the Oxford comma where appropriate.
  • Keep sentences short and focused.
  • Avoid slang, jargon, and unnecessary filler.

docs.title: Capitalization
docs.text:
Use capitalization consistently:

  • Capitalize proper nouns and official product names.
  • Capitalize headings and titles in sentence case.
  • Use lowercase for generic terms unless they begin a sentence.
  • Capitalize UI labels only when they appear as exact interface text.

docs.title: Headings
docs.text:
Use headings to create a clear hierarchy.

  • Use a single H1 per page.
  • Use H2 for major sections and H3 for supporting subsections.
  • Keep headings descriptive and scannable.
  • Avoid vague headings such as "Details" or "Info".

Example:

# Installation

## Prerequisites

### Python Version

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
Use lists to break down steps, options, or related points.

  • Use numbered lists for sequential steps.
  • Use bullet lists for related items or choices.
  • Keep list items parallel in structure.
  • Avoid nesting lists more than two levels deep.

Example:

  1. Open the project folder.
  2. Install the dependencies.
  3. Start the local server.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Use notes to call out helpful context or supporting information.

Note

Notes provide extra context that may improve understanding but is not required for the main task.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
Use warnings to highlight risks, breaking changes, or destructive actions.

Warning

Warnings should be used sparingly and only when the reader may lose data or break a workflow.

docs.title: Code Blocks
docs.text:
Code examples should be easy to copy and understand.

  • Use fenced code blocks with the correct language tag.
  • Keep examples minimal and relevant.
  • Avoid placeholder values unless they are clearly labeled.
  • Include expected output when it improves clarity.

Example:

python -m mkdocs serve

docs.title: API Writing Standards
docs.text:
When documenting APIs:

  • Describe the endpoint, method, purpose, and parameters clearly.
  • Include request and response examples.
  • Specify required headers, authentication, and error responses.
  • Use consistent naming for parameters and payload fields.
  • Mention status codes in a concise, actionable way.

Example:

  • Use: "Send a GET request to retrieve the resource."
  • Avoid: "Use the API to get data."

docs.title: Screenshot Guidelines
docs.text:
Screenshots should support the instructions, not replace them.

  • Use screenshots only when visual context is necessary.
  • Crop tightly to the relevant area.
  • Ensure the image is high resolution and readable.
  • Add descriptive alt text.
  • Label important UI elements when needed.

docs.title: Accessibility Guidelines
docs.text:
Documentation should be accessible to all readers.

  • Use descriptive headings and meaningful link text.
  • Provide sufficient contrast in diagrams and screenshots.
  • Use alt text for images and diagrams.
  • Keep tables simple and readable.
  • Avoid relying on color alone to convey meaning.
  • Write inclusive, neutral language.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: The purpose of this document is to explain the functionality of scanning QR Code from MyIndici generated by Health Kiosk.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Following are the steps to configure and show QR Code menu in Patient Portal:

  1. Login to Indici, go to Configurations -> General Configurations -> Practice -> Portal Menu section, then click on the section having menu names.
  2. A drop down will appear, then select QR Code. After selecting the QR Code, click on Update button.

  1. Go to Patients -> Search & List -> Click on the respective patient name. Patient Consult screen will be opened.
  2. Click on the Portal Registered label. A popup window will appear having Patient Portal configuration setting options.
  3. Check the QR Code checkbox under Access Settings and press Update button. Now QR Code menu will start appearing on MyIndici portal.

docs.title: QR Code Scanning
docs.text:
Following are the steps to scan QR Code from MyIndici:

  1. Login to MyIndici App. Dashboard screen will appear where QR Code option is available. This option is also available in the menu. The patient can select QR Code from either option.

  1. This will redirect user to QR Code scanning section. The following screen will appear:

  1. Now scan the QR Code by placing the app in front of printed QR Code. Make sure that camera focuses on the QR Code.
  2. After successful scanning, vitals details from the QR Code will be saved in the patient profile and a success message will appear. In the given image, we are saving Blood Pressure and Heart Rate data.

  1. Clicking on Yes will start scanning another QR Code. Clicking No will redirect the user to the dashboard.
  2. Patient cannot scan same QR Code or QR Code with same vitals on the same day. App will prompt "Same vitals data already exists."
  3. After saving vitals data from QR Code, patient can view the date in Vitals section of MyIndici. Following is the image of saved Blood Pressure and Heart Rate data in Vitals Section.

docs.title: Medical Warnings
docs.text:
Medical Warnings

Introduction

Our latest release introduces an important new feature that allows users to seamlessly pull

patient medical warning records from Health NZ into the indici system. The retrieved medical

warnings will be displayed under the "Allergies/Medical Warnings" section of the relevant

patientʼs consult screen in indici.

Requests to fetch the warnings are generated within indici using the Get NMWS Warnings

button, which triggers a backend script to display the data.

We have also provided useful filtering capabilities so users can search for medical warnings

based on specific criteria such as date and status.

Configurations to Access Medical Warnings

To enable a user to access indici Medical Warnings, the user's role access rights must be

configured at the practice level. The following steps need to be followed to display the Medical

Warnings tab on the Patient Consult screen:

  1. Log in to indici

  2. Go to Configurations > User Management > Access Rights

  3. Here you will see the Medical Warning permission. This allows you to control which user

roles have access to.

  1. Mark the checkboxes under the user roles you want to have access to and click Save:

Medical Warnings Workflow

The below steps illustrate the complete flow of how medical warnings are displayed indici:

  1. Go to Patients > Search & List:

  2. On the Search & List screen, click the name of the relevant patient to open their Consult

screen.

  1. In the left pane click the Allergies/Medical Warnings option:

  2. Click the Medical Warnings tab:

  3. To fetch medical warnings from Health NZ, click the Get NMWS Warnings button. A script is

executed in the backend, ensuring that the most up-to-date medical warnings from Health NZ

are retrieved and displayed accurately:

  1. The medical warnings retrieved from Health NZ will be displayed as highlighted in the below

image:

records:

docs.title: User Guide Overview¶
docs.text:
Welcome to the Patient Management System User Guide!!

This guide provides step-by-step instructions to help users perform common tasks within the Patient Management System. It is designed for administrative staff, receptionists, healthcare professionals, and other authorized users who manage patient information and daily operations.

The documentation explains the core workflows of the system, including patient registration, appointment scheduling, appointment management, and other essential functions. Each guide includes clear instructions to help users complete tasks accurately and efficiently.

docs.text: This User Guide contains documentation for:

docs.title: Purpose¶
docs.text: The purpose of this guide is to:

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This release introduces a series of enhancements focused on improving medication visibility, prescribing accuracy, and workflow efficiency across indici.

Several of these improvements support clearer management of long-term medications and repeat prescriptions, helping practices prepare for upcoming prescription duration changes.

Updates include improved long-term medication display, streamlined medication editing, updated prescription printing aligned with current NZePS standards, strengthened confidentiality controls, and clearer handling of stopped or cancelled medications.

Enhancements have also been made to AI usage reporting to improve transparency and cost tracking.

docs.title: Long-Term Medication Display Update
docs.text: The Long-Term Medication section in the Consult top bar has been updated to improve readability and reduce visual clutter.

docs.title: What's Changed
docs.text:
• Quantity and Duration (Q/D) are now displayed for long-term medications.
  • Medication dates are hidden by default to keep the view clean.
  • A new toggle icon allows users to show or hide dates as needed.

These changes improve clarity when reviewing long-term medications, particularly where prescriptions may cover longer intended treatment periods.

docs.title: Print Prescription Enhancement
docs.text: Prescription printing in indici has been updated to use a new standard format, changing from the previous PDF layout to an XHTML format, in line with Health NZ (HNZ) compliance requirements.

docs.title: What This Means for Your Practice
docs.text:
• Printed prescriptions may look slightly different.
  • The prescribing process and information remain the same.
  • This is a national standard format and cannot be customised or made practice-specific.

docs.title: Why This Change Was Made
docs.text:
• To meet current Health NZ compliance standards used by pharmacies.
  • To ensure consistent and reliable prescription printing across all practices.

docs.title: Confidential Medication Setting
docs.text: New options have been added to allow medications to be marked as confidential, providing greater control over how sensitive medication information is shared and accessed.

docs.title: Restricted
docs.text: Medication information is shared with the Medicine Data Repository (MDR) but is not generally visible. Access is limited to authorised users and approved MDR protocols.

docs.title: Very Restricted
docs.text:
Medication information is completely hidden and cannot be accessed or viewed in the MDR under any circumstances.

When the Confidential checkbox is selected, the confidentiality level can be chosen from a dropdown (default: Restricted).

docs.title: Medication Grid - Quick Edit Enhancement
docs.text: The Medication Grid (Today's Medication Activity list) has been enhanced to support quicker updates to active medications.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
• A new Quick Edit icon is available for current medications.
  • Users can update Quantity and Duration directly from the Today's list.
  • Changes are saved immediately after selecting Update.

Quantity and Duration updates remain subject to existing prescribing rules, medicine eligibility, and prescriber clinical judgement.

docs.title: Displaying Prescribed and Dispensed Medicine Names
docs.text: The ePS Medication History view has been enhanced with a new toggle to improve visibility of dispensing information.

docs.title: What's Changed
docs.text:
• Prescribed medicine names are shown by default.
  • A new toggle icon allows users to view dispensed medicine names.
  • Users can switch between prescribed and dispensed medicine details on demand.

docs.title: Medication Management - Delete and Stop Functionality
docs.text: The behaviour of the Delete and Stop actions has been clarified to ensure safer medication management.

docs.title: Medications with Remaining Repeats
docs.text: When stopped or deleted, the medication becomes inactive and cannot be dispensed in the future.

docs.title: Currently Active Medications
docs.text:
When deleted or stopped, the medication is marked as cancelled.

This is particularly important for prescriptions with extended repeat periods, ensuring discontinued medicines cannot be dispensed unintentionally.

docs.title: AI Credit Usage Report Enhancements
docs.text: The AI Credit Usage Report has been enhanced to provide greater visibility and improved filtering capabilities.

docs.title: AI Usage
docs.text:
A Type search filter has been added, allowing users to filter the AI Usage Report by AI Consultation - SOAP Notes or Letters & Documents.

By default, the Type filter is set to All, displaying both SOAP Notes and Letters & Documents AI usage records.

Additionally, a Type column has been added to the report grid, clearly indicating whether each AI usage record is associated with SOAP Notes or Letters & Documents.

docs.title: AI Query Builder
docs.text:
A new AI Query Builder tab has been introduced to provide detailed insights into AI query activity.

This report includes the following information:

  • Date and time of the query
  • Query title
  • Query description
  • User name
  • AI usage cost

This enhancement improves transparency and helps administrators better track AI usage and associated costs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This release includes usability-focused enhancements to reporting and referral workflows to make day-to-day operations more efficient.
